interpretation: products/pc is the entry-type HAP of the 2-in-1 product: module.json5 declares type 'entry', mainElement 'PcAbility', deviceTypes ['2in1'], form extension PhoneFormAbility (PcFormAbility.ets), PcBackupAbility, and four permissions. Responsibility: PC app shell - PcAbility sets IS_SIDEBAR_LAYOUT=true and delegates all lifecycle callbacks to BaseAbilityHelper from @ohos/abilitycommon; router_map maps 'MainPage' to PcMainPage.ets, which hosts HomeView in HdsSideBar/HdsNavDestination, tracks breakpoints and handles double back-press. Boundary: form_config.json binds widget, ArticleServiceCard, LockScreenCard, LockScreenCardLG to card sources; build-profile.json5 sets stageMode, obfuscation rules and eight targets; oh-package.json5 pins local file: deps (@ohos/common, @ohos/abilitycommon incl. deep import .../widget/viewmodel/UpdateFormData, @ohos/commonbusiness, @ohos/widgetcommon). Behavior per source: PcFormAbility routes ArticleServiceCard to UpdateFormData.init and hmos_3d_live_widget to FormRdbHelper.insertForm, schedules a 6-unit refresh in onFormEvent, cleans up in onRemoveForm; backup_config.json enables backup/restore; hypium tests are scaffolds.
limitations: The claim that the 'pc' HAP builds successfully with the eight targets declared in build-profile.json5 and applies obfuscation-rules.txt as intended is unproved: no build was executed and the hvigor pipeline was not exercised.

Claims that the form 6-unit refresh scheduling in onFormEvent, FormRdbHelper persistence, and appRecovery crash restart behave correctly at runtime on a 2-in-1 device are unproved; they rest solely on reading source, not on device or emulator observation.

The claim that the referenced exports from workspace dependencies (e.g. WidgetCardComponent and PC_ABILITY in WidgetCard.ets, TABS_LIST and HomeView from @ohos/abilitycommon) resolve under the pinned file: dependency versions is unproved because no compiler or type-checker was run over the workspace.

interpretation: IapDataModel.ets is a 52-line, logic-free declaration module that fixes the type vocabulary of the app's IAP contract. It declares PurchaseData (the JWS envelope with optional jwsPurchaseOrder/jwsSubscriptionStatus), PurchaseOrderPayload (purchase fields incl. finishStatus), the subscription chain SubGroupStatusPayload -> SubscriptionStatus -> optional lastPurchaseOrder/renewalInfo, and string-valued enums FinishStatus ('1'/'2') and SubStatus ('1','2','3','5') mirroring IAP status codes; SubRenewalInfo stays module-private. Maintenance contract: field names, optionality, and enum values are load-bearing. Pages JSON.parse IAPKit strings (after JWSUtil.decodeJwsObj base64url decoding) and blind-cast to these interfaces with no runtime validation, so renaming a field or changing an enum value silently changes consumer branching (finishStatus !== FINISHED gates finishPurchase; status === ACTIVE gates product display) instead of failing loudly. Any edit must stay in sync with IAPKit server payload shapes and all four importing pages at once, and new IAP fields belong here rather than inline in pages.
limitations: No IAPKit server payload sample or schema exists in the repository, so the claim that the interface field names and enum string values exactly match live IAP JWS payloads is inferred from consumer usage and the sample readme, not verified against the service.

The four page consumers typecast JSON.parse results to these interfaces with 'as'; whether ArkTS type checking or any runtime guard ever rejects mismatched payload shapes was not tested, as no build, compiler run, or device execution was performed.

Fields such as SubGroupStatusPayload.environment, applicationId, packageName, and historySubscriptionStatusList appear unconsumed in the current pages; whether they are reserved for future IAP features or dead declarations is unproved.

SubscriptionsPage comments mention signature verification of jwsSubscriptionStatus, but JWSUtil.decodeJwsObj only base64url-decodes; whether cryptographic JWS verification happens elsewhere is not established by this scope.

interpretation: Responsibility: Index.ets, the sole @Entry page, hosts nine Tabs whose buttons wrap one documented @kit.UserAuthenticationKit recipe each: getAvailableStatus ATL3 FACE check, four getUserAuthInstance start() flows (PIN/FACE/FINGERPRINT at ATL3, ReuseUnlockResult variants, one uiContext widget), cancel() after 3s, on('authTip') perception, getEnrolledState digest, async getAuthLockState, ATL2 companion-device flow. Boundary: keep module.json5 (srcEntries, ACCESS_BIOMETRIC + SECURITY_RESTRICTIONS), main_pages 'pages/Index', and build-profile.json5 obfuscation plus default/ohosTest targets consistent; EntryAbility seeds AppStorage 'pageContext'/'UIContext' read by resourceToString and the toast, so renaming either key desynchronizes page and ability. Relations: in-scope imports are only common/Logger plus Kits; hvigorfile.ts pins hapTasks; the ohosTest hypium suite only asserts string containment, never userAuth. Behavior: results sit in an 8-slot @State array indexed by ResultIndex; each on('result') self-unsubscribes via off('result'); challenge is 16 cryptoFramework bytes, 3 retries; Kit failures are BusinessError-logged, never rethrown; resourceToString degrades to 'undefined'.
limitations: That the ATL3 FACE/PIN/FINGERPRINT flows or companion-device flow succeed on any device is unproved: no device or emulator execution was performed, and results depend on enrollment and vendor capability not observable in the tree.

That the declared ohos.permission.ACCESS_BIOMETRIC and ohos.access.permission.SECURITY_RESTRICTIONS permissions are actually required (versus merely declared) for getAvailableStatus, getEnrolledState, or getAuthLockState is an inference from module.json5, not a verified SDK contract.

The semantics and numeric values of MAX_ALLOWABLE_REUSE_DURATION and PERMANENT_LOCKOUT_DURATION are taken from usage context only; no SDK typings were consulted, so version drift in @kit.UserAuthenticationKit is not ruled out.
The obfuscation rules in obfuscation-rules.txt were not evaluated, so whether release obfuscation preserves the reflection-sensitive ArkUS struct and JSON.stringify of AuthLockState is unverified.

interpretation: features/widgetcommon is a HarmonyOS static library ("har", module @ohos/widgetcommon) holding form-card UI reused by products: phone and pc depend on it via "file:../../features/widgetcommon" and their card pages (e.g. ArticleServiceCard.ets) instantiate its structs. Index.ets is the sole public surface: six card components (ArticleCard, LockScreenCard, LockScreenCardLG, WidgetCard, WidgetLiveCardCode, WidgetStaticCard), view models/types, constants, ALL_ARTICLE_LISTS content. Contract: expose or retire API only via Index.ets; components are @Component structs configured by abilityName and fire postCardAction router/message events carrying FormCardEnum tags, formId and articleInfo, so FormCardEnum values and param names are a cross-module contract with @ohos/common and product form abilities; ArticleCardComponent reads host LocalStorage keys 'cardList'/'formId'; components reference app.* resource ids that must stay consistent with src/main/resources; tests are scaffold placeholders, so regressions surface only in review. Cross-kit imports (@kit.ArkUI, FormKit, SensorServiceKit, BasicServicesKit) stay confined to live-widget animation and formProvider helpers.
limitations: The claim that the postCardAction params (FormCardEnum values, 'cardFrom', 'formId', 'articleInfo', 'requestOverFlow') are consumed by the products' form abilities is inferred from matching literal strings in source, not proven by tracing runtime dispatch, since no compiled or executed entry was observed.

The claim that ALL_ARTICLE_LISTS detailsUrl entries resolve to real bundled article pages inside the products is unproved: the H5/content packages referenced by those relative paths were not located or validated within this checkout.

The statement that LocalStorage keys 'cardList' and 'formId' are populated by the hosting card pages is based on reading the @LocalStorageProp declarations only; the producers of those keys in each product were not verified.

interpretation: Whole ArkTS syntax inventory exists, but current reusable semantic Skills concentrate on selected scenario paths. This is not whole-repository semantic mastery.

The devpractices feature owns sample retrieval/cache fallback and image-preview lifecycle paths. Exact imports, calls, owners and spans establish local relations and bounded behavior hypotheses, including one lexical createImagePacker/release pairing. This does not prove compiler dataflow, exception safety, UI behavior, or runtime execution.
Product entry modules own application shells; feature modules own scenario UI/business slices; common owns shared services, storage, models, components, and utilities.
The known example purchaseData flow has four verified bounded steps to consumeOwnedPurchase, but alias/object identity and runtime bridge behavior remain unresolved.
The package declares tsc without input files or a root tsconfig; npm install passes and npm run build exits 1. This is an upstream build-contract gap, not a qualified regression oracle.
Large shared SDK-import groups are expected corpus-wide. Without a project-local behavior relation and oracle, their cardinality is a false-positive risk rather than a task candidate.
The nearest independently rooted build-profile defines the initial semantic ownership boundary; module build profiles beneath it do not create cross-sample dependencies.

The SetBasicAttrsEvts sample owns the selected UserAgent_four route and its ArkWeb API-use context. Exact revision-bound localization, route calibration, a structurally distinct valid implementation, a meaningful wrong-route variant, and eight preservation routes establish a bounded page-registration and visible-semantic contract. This does not qualify the broader ArkWeb lifecycle hypothesis or unseen-Agent discrimination.
Existing deep evidence is concentrated on consumable purchaseData. Environment, other product types, navigation, JWS edge cases, and runtime account/store transitions need independent mining.
The consumable purchaseData path has seven verified local expression-flow steps through finishPurchase; external SDK behavior and app-server verification are not source-resolved.
